title: Count lines and words in a text file
description:
Write a function `count_lines_and_words(path)` that reads the text file at `path` and returns `(line_count, word_count)`.

Covers all 4 sub-parts of source item 1 (Obama's, Michelle Obama's, Donald Trump's, and Melina Trump's speeches, all real transcripts) as one exercise with 4 test cases - each file is available in your working directory.
hints: Idea to consider: read the whole file, then use splitlines() and split()

text.splitlines() breaks the text into a list of lines without keeping the newline characters; text.split() breaks it into a list of words on any whitespace. Their lengths give you the two counts directly.
Open the file, read its full contents, and return (len(text.splitlines()), len(text.split())).
expected_behavior: Returns the number of lines and the number of words in the file.
explanation: splitlines() and split() both do their own counting internally - reading the file once and calling each of them is simpler and faster than looping over the file object twice.
